JACK BIDGOOD, LEN COLEMAN and TOM COTTON donned Belgrave vests in 1929 and that great character, International and Champion runner, and Past President TOM CARTER was persuaded into the claret and gold in August 1930.

Tom Cotton, M.P. for the Battersea Park Division, is universally known for his fighting speeches in the House and his consummate command of language, and is ably supported from the back benches by A.W.

Fireman TOM COTTON is now stationed at Wimbledon but regrets he is unable to get along to the Hall. ERNIE DUFFETT, whose job as a 'copper' also keeps him away from the Hall, has a most unthankful job as a Club Handicapper, but to be paid compliments by the cross-country members is indeed a feather in his cap.

All age groups of the Club were represented but I especially noticed those from Alf's earlier days, in the 1930's, Ken O'Kell, Bill and Frank Webb, Tom Carter, Tom Morrell, Albert Shaw, Tom Cotton, Tommy Scrimshaw and many others.
The band coaxed almost everyone onto the floor, and Tom Cotton's songs were greatly appreciated. The lads performed "Little Nell" with tragic feeling.
No doubt the advertised Crazy Cabaret, produced by Tom Cotton and trained by Miss Jo Parsons, was one of the attractions, and accounted for the really fine crowd which assembled.
